title: Note On Fair Copy And Correspondence

questions.question: Why does the note say some ideas from other books were included again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because those other parts were not available there, so some important points had to be mentioned again.

questions.question: What was the treatise supposed to help the students in that area do?
questions.answer: It was meant to help them write a small but complete version of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How is the repeated material described in the note?
questions.answer: It is described as seeming like repetition on the outside.

questions.question: What kind of copy was later prepared after the first rough writing?
questions.answer: A revised copy was made from the rough draft.

questions.question: What is said about the person who wrote the revised copy?
questions.answer: He is described as blessed, even though he did not know much about these special matters.

questions.question: What special pattern was noticed in the revised copy?
questions.answer: A meaningful pattern was seen in the letters, especially in how many alifs appeared at the start of lines.

questions.question: How many alifs were counted at the beginnings of the lines?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What is an alif?
questions.answer: It is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet, written like a straight vertical line, and its number value is one.

questions.question: What title is connected to the number that was found?
questions.answer: The title is Ayat al-Kubra, which means The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: Whom does the note say gave this title to the treatise?
questions.answer: Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

questions.question: What did the matching number show about the title?
questions.answer: It showed that the title fit the treatise well.

questions.question: What other meaning was understood from this number pattern?
questions.answer: It was taken as a sign that the treatise came as a light-filled reflection from Qur’anic verses.

questions.question: What number of Qur’anic verses is mentioned in the note?
questions.answer: Six thousand six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this note?
questions.answer: It explains why some ideas were repeated and tells about a meaningful number pattern connected to the treatise’s title and its link to the Qur’an.

questions.question: Why were parts of The Words and The Flashes mentioned again in this treatise?
questions.answer: They were mentioned again because those other writings were not on hand where this treatise was written.

questions.question: Did the writers still have the students copy the whole treatise or only the new parts?
questions.answer: They had the students copy the whole treatise.

questions.question: Why did they want the students to write the whole treatise?
questions.answer: So the students in that region could produce a short but complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Was the first version polished or unfinished?
questions.answer: It was unfinished, since it is described as a rough draft.

questions.question: Who wrote the corrected version of that draft?
questions.answer: A blessed person wrote it.

questions.question: What makes the discovery in his copy surprising?
questions.answer: It is surprising because he did not know about these kinds of hidden meanings.

questions.question: What hidden feature was seen in his writing?
questions.answer: A fine and deep matching pattern in the letters was seen.

questions.question: Where exactly were the counted alifs found?
questions.answer: They were found at the starts of the lines.

questions.question: What was the total number of those alifs?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: How did that number connect with the treatise’s title?
questions.answer: It matched the abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: According to the note, what did this match prove?
questions.answer: It proved that the title suited the treatise.

questions.question: Besides the title, what else did the number seem to point to?
questions.answer: It pointed to the treatise being a shining piece drawn from the light of the Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the note mention the total number of Qur’anic verses?
questions.answer: To connect the number pattern with the Qur’an and show another meaningful sign.

questions.question: What problem existed when this treatise was being written?
questions.answer: The other parts of the Risale-i Nur were not available in that place.

questions.question: Because of that problem, what happened in this treatise?
questions.answer: Some important topics from other works were included again.

questions.question: Which two works are named as having some of their important points repeated here?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: Why did they still want everything in the present treatise written down?
questions.answer: They wanted the students there to prepare a compact but complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: After the first writing, what was produced next?
questions.answer: A revised copy was produced.

questions.question: How is the person who made that revised copy described in character and knowledge?
questions.answer: He is described as blessed in character but not learned in these special subjects.

questions.question: What careful observation was made in his copy?
questions.answer: A delicate and deep harmony in the letters was noticed.

questions.question: Which letter was counted in that pattern?
questions.answer: The letter alif.

questions.question: What was special about where those letters appeared?
questions.answer: They appeared at the beginning of the lines.

questions.question: What was the final count of those beginning letters?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What system is used in the note to compare that number with the title?
questions.answer: The abjad system, where letters have number values.

questions.question: What title had the same number value?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What conclusion was drawn from this matching value?
questions.answer: The title was seen as very fitting for the treatise.

questions.question: What second conclusion was drawn from the same number?
questions.answer: The treatise was understood as a ray from the light of the Qur’anic verses.

questions.question: What useful reason is given for including those points again?
questions.answer: The students needed a complete small collection in that area.

questions.question: What happened to the rough draft after it was first written?
questions.answer: It was revised into another copy.

questions.question: What is noteworthy about the person who revised it?
questions.answer: He was not trained in these hidden correspondences, yet something remarkable appeared in his copy.

questions.question: What remarkable thing appeared in the revised copy?
questions.answer: A subtle letter pattern was noticed.

questions.question: What letter is the focus of that pattern?
questions.answer: The alif.

questions.question: What basic facts are given about alif?
questions.answer: It is the first Arabic letter and its number value is one.

questions.question: How many of these letters were found at line beginnings?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What was that number compared with?
questions.answer: It was compared with the number value of the treatise’s title.

questions.question: What title matched that number?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: Who is mentioned in connection with that title?
questions.answer: Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

questions.question: What did the match between the count and the title suggest?
questions.answer: It suggested that the title was especially suitable.

questions.question: What larger sacred source is also linked to the number match?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is linked to it.

questions.question: How does the note connect the treatise to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says the treatise is a shining reflection drawn from the light of Qur’anic verses.

questions.question: In the note, what was missing from the place where the treatise was written?
questions.answer: Other sections of the Risale-i Nur were missing there.

questions.question: How did that affect what was written in this treatise?
questions.answer: Important subjects from some other sections were included again.

questions.question: Which students were especially being considered?
questions.answer: The students of the Risale-i Nur in that area.

questions.question: What did the writers want those students to produce?
questions.answer: A small complete collection of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What kind of draft came before the revised copy?
questions.answer: A rough draft came first.

questions.question: Who prepared the revised copy?
questions.answer: A blessed person prepared it.

questions.question: What is said about his knowledge of these symbolic matters?
questions.answer: He did not know much about them.

questions.question: What was still found in his copy even without that knowledge?
questions.answer: A deep and fine letter correspondence was found.

questions.question: Which part of the writing was counted to find this correspondence?
questions.answer: The alifs at the start of the lines were counted.

questions.question: What number was reached by that count?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What is the significance of that number in relation to the title?
questions.answer: It equals the abjad value of Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What did this equality help demonstrate?
questions.answer: It helped show that the title truly matched the treatise.

questions.question: What extra meaning was understood from the same equality?
questions.answer: It was seen as a sign that the treatise comes from the light of the Qur’an.

questions.question: If someone says the number was treated as meaningful and not accidental, would that fit the note? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Yes. The note presents the number as a sign pointing to the title and to a Qur’anic connection.

questions.question: What is the first main reason given for repeated ideas in the treatise?
questions.answer: The needed books were not available in that place.

questions.question: What is the second main reason for writing down the whole treatise anyway?
questions.answer: The students there were meant to have a complete small version of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Is the note mainly complaining about repetition or explaining it?
questions.answer: It is mainly explaining why the repetition was necessary.

questions.question: What happened after the rough draft was finished?
questions.answer: A revised copy was written.

questions.question: How is the one who wrote that revised copy described?
questions.answer: He is called a blessed person.

questions.question: What pattern was discovered in the revised copy?
questions.answer: A meaningful matching arrangement involving letters was discovered.

questions.question: Which letter appears in that arrangement?
questions.answer: The alif appears in it.

questions.question: In what place were these alifs counted?
questions.answer: They were counted at the beginnings of the lines.

questions.question: What was the exact total of those alifs?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What title had the same value in the letter-number system?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What does the note say this matching value demonstrates?
questions.answer: It demonstrates that the title is suitable for the treatise.

questions.question: What further sign was taken from this correspondence?
questions.answer: It was taken as a sign that the treatise is connected to the light of the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the note support that Qur’anic connection with a number?
questions.answer: It mentions the number six thousand six hundred and sixty-six for the Qur’anic verses.

questions.question: What is a good one-sentence summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The note explains why some material was repeated and describes a meaningful number pattern that supports the treatise’s title and its connection to the Qur’an.
